title: Enjoying Solitude and Other People
coreMove: Handle alone time and social time as skills, choosing the structure that turns isolation or contact into ordered experience.
sourcePressure: Solitude and relationship are both skill domains: loneliness, family, friendship, and community become ordered only when attention is actively shaped.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Say people just need more connection or more alone time.

sourceAnchors.name: taming solitude
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen contents list taming solitude as a Chapter 8 subheading
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Solitude has to be tamed because an empty room does not automatically become a quiet mind.

sourceAnchors.name: the wider community
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen contents list the wider community as a Chapter 8 subheading
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The wider community matters when attention gets joined to shared rules, shared care, and work larger than private mood.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: a new city resident planning her first empty Sunday
exampleSpecs.audience: adults in transition who mistake solitude for failure
exampleSpecs.stakes: the day can become either panic-scrolling or deliberate self-directed attention
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: you wake to a silent apartment and must choose between refreshing messages and setting one hard drawing exercise at the table
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You wake up before the city buses start

exampleSpecs.domain: a father changing dinner from logistics to shared challenge
exampleSpecs.audience: parents whose family time is present but scattered
exampleSpecs.stakes: everyone is in the room but attention is split into separate screens
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show the old dinner of reminders beside the night he asks each person to teach one skill from the day and keeps phones in the hallway
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Olivier noticed the family was together only on paper

exampleSpecs.domain: a graduate student choosing a friendship ritual over vague catching up
exampleSpecs.audience: students and young professionals whose friendships thin under busyness
exampleSpecs.stakes: the friendship may become nothing but postponed plans
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: her friend says they should catch up soon, and Kasia proposes a weekly repair cafe shift with a real task between them
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "We should catch up soon," Nina says from the doorway

exampleSpecs.domain: a widower testing whether a community garden gives grief a container
exampleSpecs.audience: older adults facing loneliness after loss
exampleSpecs.stakes: contact alone may feel exposing unless it has shared work
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the garden gate sticks, and Matthew predicts whether working a plot beside others will feel intrusive or quietly ordered
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The community garden gate sticks after rain

exampleSpecs.domain: a project lead rescuing a team retreat from forced bonding
exampleSpecs.audience: leaders who confuse social flow with icebreakers
exampleSpecs.stakes: the retreat could deepen trust or create awkward performance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she reviews why the icebreaker failed, then replaces it with a shared build task where roles, goals, and feedback are visible
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The unused name tags curl at the corners

exampleSpecs.domain: a nurse protecting ten minutes of solitude between shifts
exampleSpecs.audience: care workers whose alone time is invaded by rumination
exampleSpecs.stakes: without structure the break becomes replaying every patient worry
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: ask what solitude needs so it does not turn into rumination, then show her writing three breath-counts and one handoff note
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What does a quiet room need before it becomes rest?

skillTargets: turning solitude from drift into practice
using family and community without sentimental flattening

tryThisNowSpec: Before your next alone or social hour, write the one shared or solitary task that will give attention a shape.
